ai.description: This small frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct dark interorbital bar and granular skin. A key feature is the presence of small, white, glandular spots on the flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes hassanensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or cream-colored patches on the groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes hassanensis* inhabits the evergreen forests and coffee plantations of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Raorchestes hassanensis is primarily nocturnal, remaining active during the night to forage for small insects among the vegetation of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes hassanensis* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches of terrestrial eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes hassanensis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of Karnataka, India, typically found in high-elevation forest habitats within the Hassan district.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes hassanensis* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in humid forest habitats.
